kurals.tr: Arivinmai Inmaiyul Inmai Piridhinmai / Inmaiyaa Vaiyaa Thulaku
kurals.m: The want of wisdom is the greatest of all wants; but that of wealth the world will not regard as such

kurals.tr: Arivilaan Nenjuvandhu Eedhal Piridhiyaadhum / Illai Peruvaan Thavam
kurals.m: (The cause of) a fool cheerfully giving (something) is nothing else but the receiver's merit (in a former birth)

kurals.tr: Arivilaar Thaandhammaip Peezhikkum Peezhai / Seruvaarkkum Seydhal Aridhu
kurals.m: The suffering that fools inflict upon themselves is hardly possible even to foes

kurals.tr: Venmai Enappatuva Thiyaadhenin Onmai / Utaiyamyaam Ennum Serukku
kurals.m: What is called want of wisdom is the vanity which says, "We are wise"

kurals.tr: Kallaadha Merkon Tozhukal Kasatara / Valladhooum Aiyam Tharum
kurals.m: Fools pretending to know what has not been read (by them) will rouse suspicion even as to what they have thoroughly mastered

kurals.tr: Atram Maraiththalo Pullarivu Thamvayin / Kutram Maraiyaa Vazhi
kurals.m: Even to cover one's nakedness would be folly, if (one's) faults were not covered (by forsaking them)

kurals.tr: Arumarai Sorum Arivilaan Seyyum / Perumirai Thaane Thanakku
kurals.m: The fool who neglects precious counsel does, of his own accord, a great injury to himself

kurals.tr: Evavum Seykalaan Thaandheraan Avvuyir / Poom Alavumor Noi
kurals.m: The fool will not perform (his duties) even when advised nor ascertain them himself; such a soul is a

kurals.tr: Kaanaadhaan Kaattuvaan Thaankaanaan Kaanaadhaan / Kantaanaam Thaankanta Vaaru
kurals.m: One who would teach a fool will (simply) betray his folly; and the fool would (still) think himself "wise in his own conceit"

kurals.tr: Ulakaththaar Untenpadhu Illenpaan Vaiyaththu / Alakaiyaa Vaikkap Patum
kurals.m: He who denies the existence of what the world believes in will be regarded as a demon on earth
